title: Mood may feel touchy and unsettled.
caption: Mood may feel touchy and unsettled. Signals are not loud, but the southward tilt adds a small wobble that some people notice as impatience or irritability. If you feel snappy, give yourself a little extra space and keep plans simple. — Kp 2.7 • Bz -8.0 nT • Schumann 7.69 Hz (snapshot at write time)
snapshot: Geomagnetic conditions are quiet with a gentle, unsettled undertone. The magnetic field tilted south at times, which can make the body feel more reactive even without big storms. Solar wind looks typical and no solar flares were noted. A couple of CMEs were observed recently with no evidence they are aimed at us.
affects: The wired/tired pattern may show up for some. You could feel slightly keyed up while focus fades faster than usual. Muscles may carry extra tension, and patience can run thin. These effects usually come in small waves rather than all day.
playbook:
- Use slow breathing for two to five minutes
- Keep tasks smaller and add brief pauses
- Get a short daylight walk or stretch break
- Drink water and go easy on extra caffeine

fb.caption:
Mood may feel touchy and unsettled. Signals aren’t loud today, but a south-leaning magnetic field can make the body a bit jumpier even without a full-on storm. Some people may notice impatience or snappish edges, a wired/tired buzz where focus slips sooner than usual, and a little extra muscle tightness. These blips often pass in short waves rather than lasting all day.

If you feel yourself revving, try two to five minutes of slow breathing and lengthen the exhale—simple, and it tells your nervous system it’s safe to downshift. Keep your to‑dos bite‑sized with brief pauses between them, and step outside for a short daylight walk or stretch to shake off tension. Drink water and consider skipping the extra caffeine so the edge doesn’t sharpen. If irritability pops up, what’s one small way you can step back before reacting? — Gaia Eyes watches how magnetic shifts line up with mood and focus changes.
